title: Discord Rewrites Desktop and Mobile Clients in Rust Using Zed's GPU-Accelerated Rendering Framework
summary:
Discord’s CTO Stanislav Vishnevskiy recently announced rewriting its desktop and mobile clients in Rust, moving away from Electron and React Native. The project eliminates layers of abstraction to directly leverage the device’s GPU, native mobile views, and a Rust core shared across platforms. Early results hint at a significant reduction in RAM usage and boot time for chat, voice, and streaming.

By Bruno Couriol

title: LinkedIn Cuts Daily Spark Shuffle Fetch Failures from 750 to 20 with Apache Celeborn
summary:
LinkedIn deployed Apache Celeborn as a shared remote shuffle platform across most Spark and Flink workloads, reducing daily shuffle fetch failures from approximately 750 to 20. The deployment also lowered compute costs by 10%, improved application runtimes by 14%, and reduced shuffle costs per task by nearly 90% through dedicated storage, replication, and data-plane optimizations.

By Leela Kumili

title: Presentation: Behind Booking.com's AI Evolution: The Unpolished Story
summary:
Jabez Eliezer Manuel discusses the 20-year evolution of Booking.com’s data management and ML platforms. He explains how they scaled MySQL topologies, sunset Hadoop for cloud architecture, and built high-throughput model serving and feature stores operating at 400B predictions per day. He also shares insights on personalization, interleaved experimentation, and their new agentic AI foundation.

By Jabez Eliezer Manuel

title: Vercel Releases UI SDK for Agents to Compose UI from Reusable Behaviors
summary:
Vercel has released UI SDK in beta, an Apache 2.0 TypeScript library of more than 50 UI behaviors in @ui-sdk/core, with adapters for React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, and Web Components, so agents can compose accessible components and operate them through a documented agent bridge.

By Daniel Dominguez

title: AWS PrivateLink Tunnel Endpoints Open a Whole CIDR Range to Another Account
summary:
AWS has detailed tunnel endpoints, a PrivateLink endpoint type that gives a consumer VPC access to an entire network segment in another account rather than one resource at a time, over an overlapping address space and with consumer-initiated connections only. The consumer must wrap traffic in GENEVE; only TCP and DNS pass, and access logs cannot attribute traffic to a workload behind the endpoint.

By Steef-Jan Wiggers

title: Qwik 2.0 RC: Replaces HTML Comment Markers for Faster Reactivity and Out-of-Order Streaming
summary:
Qwik 2.0 Release Candidate, published on 1 October 2026, replaces v1's HTML comment markers with two script blocks that hold state and virtual node data. It adds experimental out-of-order streaming, async useComputed$, and cacheable route loaders. Qwik's benchmarks show v2 at 1.23x vanilla JavaScript, versus 2.59x for v1. A migration command is provided.

By Daniel Curtis

title: Presentation: Scaling LLM-Based Ranking Systems for Latency-Critical Search & Recommendation Workloads
summary:
Sundara Raman Ramachandran shares how LinkedIn productionizes LLM ranking under strict P99 latency SLAs. He discusses distilling a 7B model down to 400M parameters, compressing job contexts into single-token embeddings for a 10x throughput leap, and eliminating hidden system bottlenecks - from custom flash attention masks to Python GIL workarounds, gc.freeze, and non-blocking CUDA memory copies.

By Sundara Raman Ramachandran

title: Microsoft Releases .NET 11: C# 15 Union Types, Native AOT CLI Host, and CoreCLR by Default in MAUI
summary:
Microsoft has released .NET 11, a Standard Term Support release with two years of support. It ships C# 15 with union types and closed hierarchies, a Native AOT CLI host, a preview of Runtime Async, Zstandard compression, asynchronous validation and OpenAPI 3.2 in ASP.NET Core, CoreCLR as the default runtime in .NET MAUI, and EF Core 11 with experimental vector search.

By Almir Vuk

title: Ten Years On, Google Updates the SRE Book for the AI Era
summary:
Google has announced a completely rewritten second edition of Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems, ten years after the original book was published by O'Reilly Media. The update reframes SRE around modern cloud architectures, platform engineering and AI workloads, while retaining the discipline's original emphasis on applying software engineering to operations.

By Matt Saunders

title: Uber’s Legal AI Agent Cuts Contract Review Time by 20% with Rules and RAG
summary:
Uber’s Legal Redlining Agent reviews contract changes in Microsoft Word using RAG, historical lawyer feedback, and deterministic policy rules. Built with LangGraph, OpenSearch, and Redis, the system reports more than 20% lower average contract review time and 91% accuracy in AI-generated decisions. Uber is exploring agentic harnesses, skills, legal ontologies, and knowledge graphs.

By Leela Kumili
